question: Does the 2024 Navotas-Malabon-Tullahan fish survey provide usable site-linked NCR evidence, and are the reported species rows internally taxonomically consistent?
citation: Encarnacion, J., Ergino, G., Rivera, S. M., Tamula, P. K., & Dalawangbayan, R. (2024). Anthropogenic Activities, Water Quality and Ichthyofaunal Diversity of Navotas Riverine Ecosystem, Philippines. Journal of Biology and Health Science, 1(1), article 3. https://doi.org/10.56147/jbhs.1.1.3

journalVersion.access: Publisher-hosted full PDF text reviewed; article prints a 2024 copyright notice.

preprintVersion.peerReviewStatement: Preprints.org says version 2 is not peer-reviewed and identifies the journal article as a peer-reviewed version. That statement is attributed to the repository; the review does not independently evaluate the journal review process.

sourceVersions.comparison: The journal PDF and the current Preprints.org v2 agree on the three-site, January–April 2024 survey and the seven Table 6 row labels and counts. The duplicated Lutjanus argentimaculatus entry persists in the journal table; no correction or distinct taxonomic identification is provided.

studyScope.systemNameAsPrinted: Navotas-Malabon-Tullahan (NMT) Riverine System; the article also calls it the Navotas River system.
studyScope.collectionMethodAsReported: Fish were collected by fishermen using cast nets and basket traps, then said to be identified and verified by experts; no verifier names, identification protocol, or voucher/catalog numbers are reported in the reviewed article.

sites.settingAsPrinted: Estuary near Manila Bay, populated by fishermen.
sites.coordinateDecision: Retain only as a source transcription; no datum is stated and no independent waterbody-geometry crosswalk was performed.

sites.settingAsPrinted: Diverting channel of Tanza and Tangos Rivers.
sites.coordinateDecision: Retain only as a source transcription; no datum is stated and no independent waterbody-geometry crosswalk was performed.
Malformed DMS because seconds are 60; do not normalize, convert, map, or silently replace.

sourceClaims.abstractSpeciesCount: Six native and one invasive species.

duplicateBinomial.name: Lutjanus argentimaculatus
duplicateBinomial.unresolvedIssue: The article presents one identical binomial under two local names and supplies no separate identifiers, diagnostic criteria, vouchers, or correction. Do not count these as two species or merge their records without resolution.

sourceClaims.conservationLabels: Table 8 calls six taxa native and Sarotherodon melanotheron introduced; these labels remain source claims and were not independently evaluated here.

evidenceAssessment.stationCrosswalk: The table reports each row at all three numbered study sites, but the sites are settings within a connected riverine system rather than validated canonical feature IDs. Site 3 coordinate is malformed, and no geometry or administrative boundary overlay was added.
evidenceAssessment.temporalLimit: Four months of 2024 sampling at three sites is a bounded historical survey, not a current population estimate or complete NCR species inventory.
evidenceAssessment.rightsLimit: No open license was identified; no photographs, maps, figures, or tables are republished.

decision.disposition: Retain the article’s seven source rows with their original local-name labels for audit only. The duplicated Lutjanus argentimaculatus binomial and malformed Site 3 coordinate prevent reliable species-row normalization and mapped use; do not create app occurrences or photos.

regionIndexNote: This review is directly included in the NCR evidence manifest. The generated evidence index also finds an indirect CALABARZON repository-reference path through a CALABARZON review, the shared data/research/philippines/sources.json catalog, and this source record's reviewFiles link. That transitive file reach is not evidence that the Navotas survey, taxa, or sites belong to CALABARZON or are shared across the two regions.
nextActions: Seek clarification from the authors or an independent fish taxonomist on whether alakaak and kabang refer to distinct taxa, and request diagnostic records or voucher identifiers.
Resolve the printed Site 3 coordinate only from an authoritative correction or original field record; do not infer the intended coordinate.
Crosswalk the study’s local site descriptions against independently validated NCR river/estuary geometry before tying the source rows to canonical waterbody IDs.
Keep all seven rows research-only until taxon identity, station locality, and reuse terms are resolved.
